verdict.root_cause: Every sampled cart request spends essentially all its time in a single redis command: cartservice server spans have sub-millisecond self-time while each HGET/HMSET costs ~300-310ms, tightly pinned just above 300ms across three operations and ten independent traces [tr_9c9128fe81d7]. That is a fixed per-command delay floor, not queueing or error handling. The cartservice change record describes a repeating automated cycle whose middle step attaches a traffic-shaping sidecar to the cart-service network namespace with a fixed 300ms egress delay [tr_d490cbc84838] — matching the observed floor exactly. The log claims that shaper was detached ~1.6h before onset with nothing changing in the final ~78 minutes, but the 300ms signature observed at 13:48-13:49 contradicts that: either the detach was recorded without taking effect (netem qdisc left in the namespace) or an unrecorded sixth injection landed. The mechanism now is that cartservice waits ~300ms on every redis round-trip, inflating AddItem to ~604-617ms and frontend roots to ~650-927ms, with the cart hop flagged as the degrading hop in all ten traces [tr_9c9128fe81d7]. The frontend/checkout/loadgen alerts are the propagated wait, not independent faults: frontend's error ratio ran well below its baseline [tr_ab8f0ae6cf10] and cart spans completed OK [tr_9c9128fe81d7].
verdict.reasoning: Traces localise the fault to the cartservice->redis hop: caller spans exceed the cartservice server span by only 1-3ms, cartservice self-time is sub-millisecond, and sibling dependencies complete in 0-18ms in the same traces [tr_9c9128fe81d7]. The delay's shape — a ~10ms band around 300ms across operation types — rules out load-proportional queueing and indicates a fixed inserted wait, matching the 300ms egress shaper in the recurring automation cycle [tr_d490cbc84838]. It is dependency_latency, not bad_config, because the failure is the wait on a downstream call rather than a value naming a wrong address; not bad_deploy, because the hotfix image was reverted and logs show a stable non-restarting process serving traffic with no Redis connection or auth errors [tr_238549b07dda]. Frontend is not blamed: its error ratio fell versus baseline [tr_ab8f0ae6cf10] while the cart hop accounts for 33-46% of root self-time. Confidence is medium because change records and traces contradict each other on whether shaping was active, and cartservice metrics were absent under the queried label so latency, restarts and readiness were never measured [tr_312379e8d5f2].
open_questions: Is a netem qdisc or shaping sidecar actually present in the cart-service pod namespace now? No live pod state was inspected, and the change log claims removal 1.6h pre-onset.
If shaping is truly gone, is redis-cart itself imposing ~300ms per command? No redis-side metrics, logs or config were examined.
Onset is unverified: traces cover only 13:48:41-13:49:07 and cart logs were truncated mid-window [tr_238549b07dda], so nothing ties the 300ms floor to 13:47:15.

alternatives.root_cause: redis-cart itself is slow at ~300ms per command for its own reasons, with cartservice merely waiting.
alternatives.why_not: No redis was probed either way, but a near-constant 300ms floor identical to a documented injected-delay parameter [tr_d490cbc84838] favours external shaping over organic backend slowness.

alternatives.root_cause: A REDIS_ADDR override pointing cartservice at a non-default redis-cart port is adding per-call connection cost.
alternatives.why_not: A wrong address would produce connection or auth errors and failures on cart paths; logs show none and every cart span completed OK [tr_238549b07dda, tr_9c9128fe81d7].

proposal.expected_effect: Recreating the container gives cartservice a fresh network namespace, dropping any leftover netem/shaper residue. New traces should show redis HGET/HMSET self-time fall from ~300-310ms to single-digit ms, AddItem from ~604-617ms to <20ms, frontend roots back under ~300ms, and cartservice/redis no longer flagged as the degrading hop.
proposal.if_wrong: Post-restart traces still show redis commands pinned just above 300ms. That would mean the delay is not namespace residue but redis-cart itself (or a shaper re-attached by the automation cycle), and the next step is inspecting live pod/namespace state and redis-side metrics, which this system cannot do.
proposal.risk: Does not address a redis-side cause, so it costs a restart for nothing and discards cartservice's in-process cache; in-flight cart calls fail during recreate. If the automation cycle re-injects, relief is temporary and may mask the real trigger.
proposal.blast_radius: cartservice only, for the recreate duration; its callers frontend and checkoutservice see connection resets on cart calls, which surfaces to loadgenerator as brief checkout/cart errors.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Four simultaneous alerts spanning cart, checkout, and frontend point to a shared downstream failure rather than a single quiet warning, so it cannot be dismissed. The fanout through checkoutservice dependencies suggests dependency latency, but no evidence exists yet.
